headline: Breadth finally showed up — paid for by semis, borrowed from a bond rally, and still unconfirmed by credit.
summary: The index move hides the rotation. SPX +0.3% to 7744 and NDX -0.1%, but DJI +1.1%, RUT +1.4%, equal-weight RSP +1.4%, RSP/SPY +1.1% and IWM/SPY +1.1% — the first genuine breadth day in weeks. The fuel was duration: 10y -9bp to 5.10%, 5y -9bp, 30y -9bp (-17bp on the week), 10y real yields -6bp to 2.78%, TLT +1.4%. Everything rate-sensitive exploded off the floor — ITB +4.0%, XHB +3.1%, DHI +4.4%, HD +4.3%, XRT +3.7%, KRE +1.8%, NKE +5.2%. And it was funded out of the AI complex: SMH -1.0%, SOXX -0.9%, NVDA -1.8%, TSM -1.8%, AMD -1.5%. IGV/SMH +2.9% today and +8.7% on the week is the cleanest expression of what is actually happening inside tech.

What changed since yesterday: the Asia unwind stopped compounding and the dollar's break is now confirmed. KOSPI printed 6008.8, -0.4% on the day after the crash, though still -11.7% on the week and z=-1.55; EWY -11.4% weekly. DXY -0.5% to 102.0 — but note it is still +2.4% on the month with z=1.15 at the 91st percentile and EURUSD at 1.1217 sits in the 6.6th percentile of its year. Metals took the handoff instantly: gold +2.0% to 4188.6, silver +3.5%, platinum +2.1%, GDX +4.3%, GDXJ +4.6% — the largest moves on the tape. And the highest-beta liquidity gauge turned: BTC +9.0% on the month, IBIT +8.1%, MSTR +16.7% (+60.9% 3m), COIN +6.3% today, all now trend state 'turning up' from deeply depressed 52-week percentiles. That is a real change from a week of pure de-risking.

What is still wrong is the price of money. The rates composite is -59. The 30-year mortgage is 7.40%, +64bp on the month with z=1.91 and acceleration z=1.34, at the 100th percentile — homebuilders rallied 3-4% today against a cost of capital that is still accelerating higher. 3m bills at 4.28% are also at the 100th percentile, and 2s10s flattened another 4bp to 33bp (-14bp on the week, 24th percentile). MOVE rose 3.5% to 102.5 and is +22.4% on the month, while VIX at 16.46 is the 17th percentile and VIX3M at 18.49 the 9th, with SKEW at 160.45 in the 96th percentile. The bond market is paying for risk the equity market refuses to. Credit did not confirm the equity bounce: HYG/IEF -0.3% on the day, -1.0% on the week, z=-0.92. Internals remain broken beneath the one-day pop — IWM/SPY 10.7th percentile, XHB/SPY 6th, KRE/SPY 22.6th, EEM/SPY -4.8% on the month with z=-1.14. TGA at $885.8bn is +11.3% over three months with RRP at $1.2bn: no buffer left.

The inflation impulse is collapsing faster than the curve admits. RBOB -7.4% today and -12.9% on the month; WTI is -9.2% on the month with acceleration z=-2.41 even after a +1.1% day; corn -10.7% (acc z=-2.40), wheat -8.1%. 5y breakevens fell to 2.33% (-8bp on the month, 30th percentile), 10y to 2.32%. That argues the front end is the mispriced leg, not the long bond. It also leaves energy equities exposed: XLE fell 1.6% on a day crude rose, sits at the 96th percentile and 17% above its 200-day, with OIH -8.5% on the month and rolling over. Elsewhere the theme wreckage keeps deepening — REMX -18.4% on the month at the 0th percentile, NLR -10.9% (2.8th), URA -13.5%, TAN at the 0.4th percentile — while health care goes the other way: XLV +6.1% on the month at the 100th percentile with relative strength turning up, LLY +3.5%, UNH +9.6% on the week.

good.text: Breadth finally paid: RSP +1.4%, RUT +1.4%, RSP/SPY +1.1% and IWM/SPY +1.1% on the day, with MDY turning up on acceleration z=0.88. One day does not fix a 10th-percentile ratio, but it is the first broad participation since the de-rating began.

Duration relief across the whole curve: 10y -9bp to 5.10%, 30y -17bp on the week, 10y real yields -6bp to 2.78%, TLT +2.7% weekly and LQD +0.8% — the first time this month the long end has given equities oxygen.

The inflation impulse is deflating in real time: gasoline -7.4% today and -12.9% on the month, WTI -9.2% monthly with acceleration z=-2.41, corn -10.7%, and 5y/10y breakevens rolling over to 2.33%/2.32%. That is the disinflation the front end has not priced.

Health care is the only sector with a clean, accelerating trend: XLV +1.9% today, +6.1% on the month, z=1.37, 100th percentile, relative strength turning up. LLY +3.5%, UNH +8.2% on the month, IHI +5.7% on the week, IBB +2.0%.

Crypto turned as a bloc — BTC +9.0% on the month, IBIT +8.1%, SOL +9.3%, MSTR +16.7%, COIN +6.3% today — all from bottom-third 52-week percentiles. The most liquidity-sensitive asset on the board stopped going down first.

Dollar off the highs for a second day (DXY -0.5% to 102.0) and the precious complex reflated hard: gold +2.0%, silver +3.5%, platinum +2.1%, GDX +4.3%, GDXJ +4.6%, GDX/gold +2.5% off a z=-0.82 washout.

bad.text: The cost of money is still tightening even as yields fell. The 30y mortgage is 7.40%, +64bp on the month with z=1.91 and acceleration z=1.34 at the 100th percentile; 3m bills at 4.28% are also at the 100th percentile. Today's homebuilder squeeze (ITB +4.0%) is fighting that.

Hedges are mispriced against visible stress. MOVE +3.5% today and +22.4% on the month, SKEW 160.45 at the 96th percentile and +7.5% on the week, versus VIX 16.46 (17th percentile) and VIX3M 18.49 (9th). The term structure is turning up at 0.890.

Credit refused to confirm the equity bounce: HYG/IEF -0.3% on a +1.4% small-cap day, -1.0% on the week with z=-0.92; HYG -1.2% on the month at the 38th percentile; BKLN z=-0.68. Risk appetite in cash bonds is not following the screens.

The AI/power theme periphery keeps getting destroyed under a flat index: SOXX -8.6% and SMH -8.0% on the week, AMD -9.4%, MU -10.1%, TSM -7.8%; REMX -18.4% on the month at the 0th percentile, NLR -10.9% (2.8th), URA -13.5%, TAN at the 0.4th.

EM FX is cracking where nobody is looking: USDMXN +7.6% on the month with z=2.82 and acceleration 1.70, USDBRL +1.4% today, EWZ -2.4%, EEM/SPY -4.8% monthly (z=-1.14), Turkey -13.4% on the month. CEW's +0.5% day is complacent against that.

Energy equities have stopped marking to the barrel: XLE -1.6% on a day WTI rose 1.1%, still 96th percentile and 17% above its 200-day; XOP -1.5%, OIH -8.5% on the month and rolling over. That is distribution, not consolidation.

trades.name: 2s30s steepener
trades.line: 2s30s steepener: long front end, short the long bond
trades.expr: Long 2y futures (TU) vs short ultra-bond (WN), DV01-matched. Cash proxy: long SHY / short TLT at 4:1 notional.
trades.thesis: The curve keeps bull-flattening into a disinflating commodity complex. With 3m bills at 4.28% (100th percentile) and 5y breakevens at 2.33%, the front end carries the repricing optionality; the long end is capped by a MOVE index +22.4% on the month and a 5.43% 30y that term premium won't let rally far.
trades.trigger: 2s10s -4bp today and -14bp on the week to 33bp (24th percentile) while gasoline fell 7.4% and WTI is -9.2% monthly with acceleration z=-2.41. The disinflation is in spot, not in the bill.
trades.stop: 2s10s closes below 20bp, or 3m bills print above 4.40% — a Fed that stays frozen kills the long leg.
trades.target: 2s10s back to 55-60bp (where it sat before the 38bp YTD flattening).

trades.name: Long XLV / short XLF
trades.line: Long XLV vs short XLF - only clean sector trend vs a broken one
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long XLV / short XLF. Higher-beta version: long LLY + UNH vs short KRE.
trades.thesis: Health care is the only sector with price, momentum and relative strength all aligned, and it is working without the market's help. Financials' relative strength is rolling over with the curve flat at 33bp and regional banks at the 22nd percentile versus the S&P.
trades.trigger: XLV +1.9% today, +5.4% on the week, +6.1% on the month, z=1.37, 100th percentile of its 52-week range, relative strength +3.9% 1m and turning up. XLF relative strength is -4.5% 1m / -5.2% 3m and rolling over; KRE is -5.3% on the month despite today's +1.8% bounce.
trades.stop: XLV 1-month relative strength turns negative, or KRE/SPY reclaims its 200-day (+7% from 0.0904).

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Software over semis: long IGV, short SMH
trades.expr: Long IGV / short SMH, equal dollar. Single-name version: long MSFT vs short AVGO.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is de-rating at the capex-intensive end while the software end re-rates. IGV/SMH is only at the 32nd percentile after a -41% year — the mean reversion has barely started, and the hardware names still carry the crowded positioning.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +2.9% today and +8.7% on the week; SOXX -8.6% and SMH -8.0% weekly, NVDA -1.8%, TSM -1.8%, AMD -9.4% on the week. IGV meanwhile is +3.8% on the month and +17.0% over three months.
trades.stop: SMH closes above last week's high, or IGV/SMH falls back under the 20th percentile (roughly -5% on the ratio).

trades.name: Short XLE
trades.line: Short XLE: 96th-pctile energy vs a -9% month in crude
trades.expr: Short XLE outright, or buy 3-month 5% OTM XLE puts. Crude-neutral version: short OIH vs long XOM.
trades.thesis: Energy equity is the most crowded cyclical long on the board and it has stopped responding to the commodity. XLE sits 17% above its 200-day at the 96th percentile after a +51.8% YTD run while the barrel is decelerating sharply.
trades.trigger: XLE -1.6% and XOP -1.5% on a day WTI rose 1.1%. WTI is -9.2% on the month with acceleration z=-2.41, Brent -2.9%, RBOB -12.9%; OIH is -8.5% on the month with relative strength -10.4%.
trades.stop: WTI turns positive month-over-month with XOP making a new 52-week high.

trades.name: Long gold miners (GDX)
trades.line: Long GDX: dollar rolling, real yields down, miners +4.3%
trades.expr: Long GDX, with GDXJ for a higher-beta sleeve; or 3-month GDX 10% OTM calls to cap the downside.
trades.thesis: The miners were liquidated into the dollar spike and are snapping back faster than the metal. A DXY that has lost momentum plus 10y real yields off 6bp restores the whole bull case without needing gold to make a new high.
trades.trigger: GDX +4.3% and GDXJ +4.6% today, the biggest moves on the tape, with gold +2.0% to 4188.6 and silver +3.5%. GDX/gold +2.5% off a z=-0.82 washout; GDX is only 4.4% below its 200-day after a -7.6% month. DXY -0.5% for a second session.
trades.stop: DXY makes a new month high (above the +2.4% monthly peak) or gold closes below its month's low — the dollar squeeze resuming voids this.
trades.target: GDX +15%, retesting the 3-month high (miners are still +21.9% over 3m).

trades.name: SPX put spread - own cheap vol, sell the fat tail
trades.line: Buy 3m SPX put spread: VIX 17th pctile, SKEW 96th
trades.expr: Buy ~3-month SPX 97% puts, sell 90% puts, 1x1, for roughly 1-1.5% of notional. Skew is paying you to sell the wing.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced for calm while bond vol and tail demand scream. VIX3M at 18.49 is the 9th percentile of the year — carry is cheap — and SKEW at the 96th percentile means the OTM wing finances most of the structure. You want convexity on while the index is 6.6% above its 200-day.
trades.trigger: MOVE +3.5% today to 102.5, +22.4% on the month; SKEW +7.5% on the week to 160.45; VIX term structure turning up at 0.890; HYG/IEF -1.0% on the week with z=-0.92 while SPX printed a new high-percentile close at the 95th.
trades.stop: VIX term structure back below 0.85 with HYG/IEF making new highs — then you are paying carry into a melt-up; cut at half premium.
trades.target: VIX 24+ / 3-5x on the structure if SPX retests its 200-day 6.6% lower.

trades.name: Long USD/MXN
trades.line: Long USD/MXN: +7.6% month, z=2.82, local equities asleep
trades.expr: Long USD/MXN spot or 3-month USD calls; equity-market proxy is a short in EWW against long SPY.
trades.thesis: The peso is breaking with the single largest z-score in the FX block while Mexican equities rally — a divergence that historically resolves through the equity. Carry unwinds move faster than local index investors reprice.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +7.6% on the month, z=2.82, acceleration z=1.70, trend turning up, 5.6% above its 200-day — yet MXX rose 1.3% and EWW 1.6% today, and CEW gained 0.5%. USDBRL +1.4% on the day confirms LatAm FX pressure is broadening.
trades.stop: USDMXN closes back below 17.80, back toward its 200-day.
